item.title: Jensen Huang Returns, TrumpCare, Woke Socialism
item.description:

Next, they react to Robert Pattinson's selection as the new James Bond, and Christian pans the 2021 film No Sudden Move . Turning back to politics, the boys discuss Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's (D–Mich.) proposal for TrumpCare and Meagan Day's New York Times article on Woke 1.0. The episode wraps up with an extended discussion of the Democrats' 2027 debate schedule and the (limited) usefulness of our primary system. item.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
item.description:
The Solomon Islands scrapped a security pact with China in favor of one with Australia , a reversal that dealt a major blow to Beijing’s efforts to expand its influence in the Pacific. The 2022 agreement allowed China to rotate police training teams through the Solomon Islands, sparking alarm in Washington and Canberra, which feared China was deepening a foothold in the region. Australia has in recent years contested that effort, strengthening ties with Pacific nations including Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu with its own deals. “From China’s closest friend in the Pacific to one of Australia’s,” The Economist’s Asia diplomatic editor posted on X of the Solomon Islands’ decision, “ a big shift and an impressive piece of diplomacy .” — Prashant Rao

item.title: Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation?
item.description:
China is investigating a member of the country’s Politburo over “serious violations of discipline and law,” state media reported Tuesday, intensifying the deepest purge of Beijing’s political elite in decades. Though “we have no idea what got him in trouble ,” Shanghai Communist Party chief Chen Jining’s probe marks the first time since 1976 that four members of the Politburo have been investigated, China watcher Bill Bishop noted; others argued the move was unmistakably a continuation of Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s efforts to ensure his rule by eliminating potential successors. Xi has also purged top military leaders, calling into question the gap “between the PLA’s parade-ground precision and its battlefield readiness ,” The Wall Street Journal’s chief China correspondent wrote. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
item.description:
China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.

item.title: El Niño-fueled king tides batter California’s coast — what is the state doing about it?
item.description:
California spent two months preparing for El Niño. This week, as king tides and a powerful Thanksgiving winter storm batter the coast, the state will find out if it is ready. In September, Gov. Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of emergency for El Niño. In the proclamation and subsequent executive orders , he directed agencies to speed up permits, move supplies and people and suspend some of the state’s own rules. The state Office of Emergency Services and Department of Water Resources asked operators of levees and dams to inspect facilities ahead of the storm. The state agencies prepared sandbags, portable flood barriers and materials for emergency repairs. The state is also deploying swiftwater rescue vehicles, boats and other specialized equipment. item.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
item.description:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg . The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile , Cisco, and Motorola. The Department of Justice's 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company's CFO, Wanzhou Meng , whom the agency accused of fraud. item.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
item.description:
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. Eleven days. One Scaramucci. There’s milk in my refrigerator that was bought before Jensen Huang’s downfall, and I may pour a glass to mark his return. To review: Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after revelations that he’d had an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Huang allegedly also had an affair with an executive who was one of his 60 direct reports at Nvidia. Five days after the resignation, Nvidia’s board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company “ does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO .” Five days after that, President Trump posted that he hoped it would. This morning, citing “input from senior levels of the United States government,” the board voted unanimously to let him come back. So…
